title: Vetala Extended Tale 82: The Two Navigators and the Southern Star

full_text:
Vikram retrieved the corpse and marched on. The Vetala asked:

"Two merchant captains, Varaha and Shankha, sailed across the Indian Ocean with fleets laden with spices. Captain Varaha was boastful and proud, relying entirely on his new bronze astrolabe and ignoring the ancient seasonal wisdom of the monsoon winds. He set sail during the dark fortnight despite warning cloud formations.

Captain Shankha was humble. He observed the flight of migratory terns, studied the smell of the sea spray, and steered by the steady guidance of the Pole Star and the Southern Cross, waiting patiently for safe wind currents.

A catastrophic typhoon struck the open sea. Varaha's fleet was smashed against hidden coral reefs, losing cargo and crew. Shankha's fleet navigated through safe deep channels and arrived at the spice port in safety and triumph.

Tell me, Vikram: what was Varaha's fatal flaw—lack of technology or excess of pride?"

King Vikramaditya answered: "Excess of pride was his fatal flaw. Tools and instruments are valuable only when guided by humility and respect for the overwhelming power of nature. When pride blinds a captain to warning signs, disaster is inevitable."

"Truth speaks through you!" laughed the Vetala, and vanished into the tree.
moral: Arrogance on the ocean of life leads to shipwreck; humility and watchfulness preserve the vessel.
